query: How to construct SparsePauliOp from Pauli strings and coefficients
answer: Use qiskit.quantum_info.SparsePauliOp. Common constructors: (1) SparsePauliOp.from_list([(label, coeff), ...]) where label is e.g. "ZZ", "IX", coeff can be complex; auto-infers num_qubits. (2) SparsePauliOp.from_sparse_list([(paulis, indices, coeff), ...], num_qubits) to build from non-identity subsets; raises QiskitError on duplicate indices or out-of-range indices. (3) SparsePauliOp(PauliList([...]), coeffs) or SparsePauliOp(Pauli("Z")) for single terms. After construction you can: - simplify(atol, rtol) to combine duplicates/remove zeros; - to_list()/to_sparse_list()/label_iter() to inspect; - group_commuting(qubit_wise=False|True) to partition commuting sets for measurement; - noncommutation_graph(qubit_wise) to build grouping graph. Warning: from_sparse_observable may blow up to 2^n terms for projector inputs. Ensure Hermitian coefficients for measurement use.

query: Create PauliSumOp and convert to SparsePauliOp for measurement
answer: Preferred measurement type is SparsePauliOp. If you use opflow PauliSumOp, instantiate from a SparsePauliOp: from qiskit.opflow import PauliSumOp; h = PauliSumOp(SparsePauliOp.from_list([...])). For measurement/primitives, convert back via h.primitive (the underlying SparsePauliOp). Algorithms like PhaseEstimationScale.from_pauli_sum accept a SparsePauliOp directly and compute bounds from sum of |coeffs|. In Aer, PauliError/PauliLindbladError demonstrate conversion through SparsePauliOp(...).simplify(). Note: opflow is deprecated; for new code generate and pass SparsePauliOp directly for measurements.

query: Build fermionic observable and map to qubit using qiskit-nature
answer: Create a second-quantized operator (e.g., FermionicOp) then choose a mapper from qiskit_nature.second_q.mappers (JordanWignerMapper, BravyiKitaevMapper, BravyiKitaevSuperFastMapper, DirectMapper, LinearMapper, LogarithmicMapper, ParityMapper). Map to qubits via mapper.map(second_q_op) which returns a SparsePauliOp. With ParityMapper, pass num_particles=... to enable built-in two-qubit reduction (previously via QubitConverter(two_qubit_reduction=True)). Inspect resulting Pauli strings with for pauli, coeff in sorted(op.label_iter()). The output SparsePauliOp is ready for measurement or further grouping.

query: Best practices for grouping Pauli measurements to reduce shots
answer: Partition observables into commuting groups using SparsePauliOp.group_commuting(qubit_wise=False|True) to measure each group in a common basis, then sum weighted results. For sampling-based solvers (e.g., SamplingVQE), pass auxiliary operators as SparsePauliOp or dict/list of them; non-diagonal single-Pauli observables may raise on samplers expecting diagonal (tests show ValueError for a non-diagonal Pauli with SamplingVQE). Use label_iter()/noncommutation_graph to aid grouping and simplify() to merge duplicates before grouping. Measure each group with the appropriate basis-change (H/S) on qubits indicated by X/Y terms.

query: Convert second-quantized fermionic operators to PauliSumOp via mappers
answer: Map second-quantized operators to qubits with qiskit-nature mappers: mapper = ParityMapper(num_particles=... ) (or JordanWignerMapper, BK, BKSuperFast, Direct, Linear, Logarithmic); qubit_op = mapper.map(ferm_op) -> SparsePauliOp. If you specifically need PauliSumOp (opflow), wrap: from qiskit.opflow import PauliSumOp; pauli_sum = PauliSumOp(qubit_op). Prefer using the returned SparsePauliOp directly in modern Qiskit; two-qubit reduction is integrated in ParityMapper via num_particles.

query: Extract expectation value from Estimator for Pauli operators
answer: Aer and primitives expect Pauli or SparsePauliOp. Aer save instructions convert inputs to SparsePauliOp and require Hermitian operators; non-Hermitian raises ValueError. Example: circuit.save_expectation_value(SparsePauliOp.from_list([(“ZZ”, 1.0)]), label). For state objects, DensityMatrix.expectation_value supports Pauli and SparsePauliOp by summing per-term expvals. Algorithm results (e.g., VQD/VQE) return aux_operators_evaluated as ordered lists/dicts of expectation values (and metadata/variances). For function design: return SparsePauliOp observables; downstream Estimator/Sampler code will bind circuits and extract expvals; document that inputs must be Hermitian and optionally grouped for efficiency.
